query: How should clothing insulation, activity/metabolic rate, hydration, caffeine/medication be measured or controlled in wearable biosensing to reduce physiological confounders?

response.query: How should clothing insulation, activity/metabolic rate, hydration, caffeine/medication be measured or controlled in wearable biosensing to reduce physiological confounders?
response.answer: Clothing insulation, activity/metabolic rate, hydration, and caffeine/medication can be controlled in wearable biosensing by using sensors for thermal comfort, heart rate monitoring, sweat analysis, and microfluidic hydrogels respectively.

results.title: A new human metabolic rate sensing model optimization and wearable sensor realization - ScienceDirect
results.content: # A new human metabolic rate sensing model optimization and wearable sensor realization. The metabolic rate wearable sensor is designed based on the proposed theoretical model. Accurate assessment of metabolic rate is crucial for predicting human thermal comfort. This paper optimizes our previously proposed theoretical approach for wearable metabolic rate measurement that incorporates heart rate, whole-body unit heat loss, skin resistance, and body muscle percentage. Typically, six factors are used to evaluate thermal comfort, including four environmental parameters - air temperature, radiant temperature, air speed, and humidity and two personal parameters - metabolic rate and clothing insulation [1]. It has also been suggested [8,9] that personal parameters, such as metabolic rate and clothing insulation, play a crucial role in accurately determining thermal comfort, and this result is supported by sensitivity analysis. In addition to PMV calculation, several attempts have been made [10,11] to demonstrate the significance of metabolic rate in developing thermal comfort-related models through heat balance. [24] developed a wearable sweat rate sensor that utilizes miniaturized thermo-pneumatic actuators to measure human thermal comfort. In our previous work [30,31], which was the first of its kind, we proposed a fundamental metabolic theoretical framework based on local unit heat loss, heart rate, skin resistance and body muscle rate, showing real potential for improvement. Metabolic rate is a central parameter in accurately evaluating thermal comfort and energy saving in buildings, however, it still faces several challenges. Additionally, despite the rapid development of wearable technology, there is a lack of fundamental research models and solid methods for measuring metabolic rate in a wearable manner. This marks our initial attempt at achieving portable measurements of human metabolic rate and proposing a model with easy-to-measure physiological parameters. Accurate and portable measurement of metabolic rate can greatly contribute to the precise assessment and enhancement of human thermal comfort, as well as improving work efficiency. This research proposes a wearable metabolic rate sensor that is miniaturized, integrated, and capable of real-time measurement, while also providing comfort to the wearer. ### Study on the allowable fluctuation ranges of human metabolic rate and thermal environment parameters under the condition of thermal comfort. ### Sensitivity study for the PMV thermal comfort model and the use of wearable devices biometric data for metabolic rate estimation.

Wearable sweat sensors have gained tremendous attention on account of performing noninvasive and real-time monitoring of sweat analytes, providing a view of the human physiological state at the molecular level. Caffeine is a methylxanthine alkaloid, and its levels in the human body are directly related to health. Developing a wearable device for dynamically assessing caffeine levels in sweat could facilitate real-time personalized health monitoring. In this study, we introduced a wearable agarose hydrogel based sensor integrated with a microfluidic module for the real-time tracking of caffeine in sweat. The hydrogel based caffeine sensor demonstrated highly sensitive detection of caffeine over a broad range from 4 nM to 18.2 μM and showed a low detection limit of 1 nM. On-body tests confirmed the ability of the hydrogel based sensor to detect sweat caffeine levels continuously and dynamically, which offers a novel strategy for the instantaneous monitoring of sweat biomarkers, making it promising for subsequent daily personalized health management. ## MeSH terms. ## Substances. ## LinkOut - more resources. ### Full Text Sources. ### Medical. results.title: Rockley Photonics begins sampling biosensing wearable
results.content: The Medical Device Business Journal — Medical Device News & Articles | MassDevice. # Rockley Photonics begins sampling biosensing wearable. Rockley Photonics Bioptx biosensing band. Oxford, England-based Rockley Photonics designed its band with short-wave infrared (SWIR) biosensing technology. The company incorporated the SWIR spectrophotometer into a wearable wristband capable of several days of measurement. According to a news release, the band provides the continuous collection of spectral data. Rockley Photonics combined it with its Developer API to enable real-time monitoring of vital physiologic parameters. “We are thrilled to usher in the next generation of health monitoring with wearable laser-based technology,” Rockley Photonics Chair and CEO Dr. Andrew Rickman said. “Rockley has created the full technology stack from the design of the PIC, which forms the miniature spectrophotometer, to the full wearable integration and novel biomarker delivery. Title: Wearable Sensors for Monitoring the Physiological and Biochemical Profile of the Athlete
